hikes.name: The Crack
hikes.notes: Iconic Killarney hike — scramble through a crack in the quartzite ridge with views of Georgian Bay

hikes.name: Granite Ridge Trail
hikes.notes: Short trail with great panoramic views of the La Cloche Mountains

hikes.name: Cranberry Bog Trail
hikes.notes: Boardwalk trail through a floating bog — unique ecosystem

hikes.name: Chikanishing Trail
hikes.notes: Beautiful Georgian Bay shoreline walk over smooth granite

swimming: Topaz Lake (accessed via The Crack trail)
paddling: George Lake — easy paddle, canoe/kayak rentals available
Killarney Lake — stunning turquoise water, portage required from George Lake
tips: The Crack parking lot fills up early in summer — go before 9 AM
Bugs are intense in June/early July, bring DEET or permethrin
Park store at George Lake has firewood, ice, basic supplies
Cell service is spotty — download offline maps
Nearest full grocery: Killarney village (20 min from park gate)

hikes.name: Abes and Essens Trail
hikes.notes: Challenging day hike with views of Mazinaw Lake — can do shorter sections

hikes.name: Shield Trail
hikes.notes: Interpretive trail through Canadian Shield landscape

hikes.name: High Pines Trail
hikes.notes: Nice walk through towering white pines

swimming: Mazinaw Lake — at the beach near the campground
paddling: Mazinaw Rock — paddle right up to the 100m cliff face to see 260+ Indigenous pictographs
Upper and Lower Mazinaw Lake — full day canoe trip
tips: Take the canoe to Mazinaw Rock early morning for the best light on the pictographs
The Mugwump ferry (free) takes you to the cliff base trail
Nearest town: Cloyne (15 min) or Northbrook (20 min) for basics
Fire ban status varies — check before you go

hikes.name: Lookout Trail
hikes.notes: Short steep climb to a stunning lookout — one of Algonquin's best views

hikes.name: Track and Tower Trail
hikes.notes: Abandoned railway, lookout tower, great fall colours

hikes.name: Booth's Rock Trail
hikes.notes: Rock Lake views, old homestead ruins, cliff-top lookout

hikes.name: Centennial Ridges Trail
hikes.notes: Two high ridges with panoramic views — arguably the best hike in the park

swimming: Canisbay Lake — sandy beach at the campground
Lake of Two Rivers beach — popular swimming spot on Hwy 60
paddling: Canisbay Lake — calm, good for beginners
Canoe Lake — access to iconic Algonquin backcountry
The Portage Store at Canoe Lake for canoe/kayak rentals
tips: Algonquin Visitor Centre on Hwy 60 is worth a stop — great exhibits and bookstore
Algonquin Outfitters for gear rental
Best chance of moose: dawn/dusk along Hwy 60 corridor
Gallery Café in Dwight (20 min west) is a local favourite
Huntsville (45 min west) for full grocery/supplies

hikes.name: Cedar Sands Trail
hikes.notes: Walk through rare freshwater dune ecosystem

hikes.name: Outlet River Trail
hikes.notes: Flat trail along the Outlet River — good for birding

swimming: Sandbanks Beach (Dunes Beach) — massive sand dunes, bigger waves
Lakeshore Beach — also known as North Beach, just outside the park
paddling: East Lake — calm water, good for kayaking
West Lake — a bit bigger, also calm
tips: Sandbanks is the hardest park to book in Ontario — plan way ahead
Prince Edward County wineries are nearby — great for a day off
Picton (15 min) has great restaurants and shops
Beach gets packed on weekends — go early for parking

hikes.name: Lookout Point Trail
hikes.notes: Views over Georgian Bay from rocky outcrops

hikes.name: Twin Points Trail
hikes.notes: Shoreline trail through windswept pines — the classic Killbear experience

hikes.name: Lighthouse Point Trail
hikes.notes: Beautiful coastal walk with swimming access

swimming: Harold Point Beach — the main sandy beach
Lighthouse Point — rocky shoreline, great for snorkelling
paddling: Georgian Bay shoreline — stunning but watch for wind/waves
Killbear to Parry Sound for advanced paddlers
tips: Killbear is famous for its windswept white pines and Georgian Bay sunsets
Watch out for Massasauga rattlesnakes — Ontario's only venomous snake (rare, shy)
Parry Sound (25 min) for groceries and supplies
Bobby Orr Hall of Fame in Parry Sound if it rains

hikes.name: Stubb's Falls Trail
hikes.notes: Scenic waterfall on the Big East River — great any season

hikes.name: Homesteader's Trail
hikes.notes: Walk through old homestead area with interpretive signs

hikes.name: Beaver Meadow Trail
hikes.notes: Wetland boardwalk — good for wildlife and birding

swimming: Arrowhead Lake beach — sandy beach with shallow entry
paddling: Arrowhead Lake — small, calm, good for beginners
Big East River — gentle current, good for a lazy paddle
tips: Huntsville (15 min south) for all supplies and restaurants
The fire tower lookout is accessible in summer for panoramic views
Great base camp for exploring the Muskoka region

hikes.name: Gut Lake Trail
hikes.notes: Beautiful trail connecting small lakes

hikes.name: Swan Lake Trail
hikes.notes: Scenic walk past beaver dams and marshes

hikes.name: Beaver Dam Trail
hikes.notes: Family-friendly trail through wetlands

swimming: Grundy Lake — clear water, smooth rock shoreline
Natural rock waterslides between Gut Lake and Grundy Lake — very popular!
paddling: Grundy Lake — good for casual paddling
Canoe route connecting multiple lakes in the park
tips: The natural waterslides are a highlight — smooth granite channels between lakes
Campground is very family-friendly
Britt (15 min) has a gas station; Parry Sound (30 min) for full groceries
Excellent stargazing — relatively low light pollution
